verdict.root_cause: frontend's gRPC client logs are the only mechanism-naming signal on the board: repeated status 13 INTERNAL responses received from the product catalog dependency, whose detail text attributes the failure to a deliberately enabled 'fail' feature flag, recurring at 06:10:38 and 06:10:47 [tr_b041e95a699e]. The frames arise in the client status-receive path, so frontend is relaying an error handed to it, not generating one. That makes productcatalogservice the failing party: a feature flag governing its catalog lookups is set to a value that makes it return INTERNAL, and the wrongness of that value is itself the failure — no timeout, deadline or capacity language appears, and traces in the same minutes show nothing slower than a 26ms end-to-end checkout [tr_b8fd3c6f3d15]. The flag is absent from productcatalogservice's own change log, which is empty for 24h [tr_41fdb1b0dad1], consistent with it living in the separate FeatureFlagService visible in the trace tree [tr_b8fd3c6f3d15]. The fix is to flip the flag off, not to roll back or restart.
verdict.reasoning: Only [tr_b041e95a699e] produced a positive observation: a remote status, a named dependency, an explicit fault-injection reason, and recurrence — which internally rules out transient, timeout and resource-limit readings. Everything else is empty or negative. The low aggregate error ratios for productcatalogservice [tr_bb247e5cb0de] and frontend [tr_ab4785ce0d4c] are unbroken service-wide series over noisy baselines, so a flag affecting one RPC path need not lift them, but they do not corroborate either. The callee's own logs were never actually read: the selector used a hyphenated label that does not match the service name [tr_e668a04490f1]. adservice's only changes are matched memory-limit apply/revert pairs, the last restoring the cap 1.9h before onset [tr_93af46dee0e9], so no lowered limit was in force; its metrics are vacuously empty in both windows [tr_2f7cde204b26]. Not bad_deploy because no artifact changed; not dependency_latency because the failure is an immediate INTERNAL, with the slowest hop ~6-7ms [tr_b8fd3c6f3d15]; not resource_exhaustion because the only capacity-shaped change was already reverted.
open_questions: The trace sample spans 06:10:21-06:10:57 with zero error spans across 94 spans [tr_b8fd3c6f3d15], yet the flag-attributed errors are logged inside that same minute [tr_b041e95a699e] — sampling gap or different path, unresolved, and the main reason confidence is not high.
productcatalogservice's own logs were never read due to a label mismatch [tr_e668a04490f1]; re-querying with the correct label would confirm or overturn the flag on the callee side.

Where the flag lives, who flipped it and when is unestablished — no dispatch queried the feature-flag service's change history, so the 06:09 onset is not time-correlated to any recorded act [tr_41fdb1b0dad1].

alternatives.root_cause: The frontend->adservice edge is failing or timing out and drives the incident, unseen because that edge is entirely unmeasured.
alternatives.why_not: No positive evidence at all: no sampled span [tr_b8fd3c6f3d15] and no metric series in either window [tr_2f7cde204b26]. It is unmeasured rather than implicated, and no error text names it, whereas the catalog flag is named explicitly.

alternatives.root_cause: adservice is being OOM-killed under a lowered 256m memory cap, degrading the ad path frontend depends on.
alternatives.why_not: The last recorded change restored the memory limit ~1.9h before onset, so the cap was not in force at 06:09, and nothing landed in the minutes before onset [tr_93af46dee0e9].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The observation that would justify a later proposal is a productcatalogservice log query under the correct label (the earlier attempt used 'product-catalog-service' and returned zero lines [tr_e668a04490f1]) showing server-side INTERNAL responses attributed to the fail flag at 06:10:38 and 06:10:47, plus a change-history entry naming the flag flip on whichever service actually holds it.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the flag is in fact stored in productcatalogservice's own environment and simply not journalled — in that case revert_config on productcatalogservice would clear the status 13 INTERNAL lines from frontend's log within a minute and the abstention cost an easy fix. It is also wrong if a runbook (withheld from this briefing) names an approved flag-reset path I could not see. The correct next step is a dispatch, not an action: re-query productcatalogservice logs with the label value 'productcatalogservice', and query change history for the FeatureFlagService named in the trace tree [tr_b8fd3c6f3d15].
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the fail flag set, so catalog lookups keep returning INTERNAL to frontend and the user-visible errors continue until someone acts manually. That is a real cost, accepted because the alternative is acting on an unmet precondition. Had I proposed revert_config on productcatalogservice, the risk would be recreating a service whose recorded prior configuration is empty — restoring it to an unknown or default environment, potentially changing dependency addresses that currently work, and dropping its in-process cache, all while leaving the flag untouched because the flag is held elsewhere.
proposal.blast_radius: Nothing changes, so nobody sees a change. The unremediated fault continues to be seen by frontend (which logs the relayed status 13), by checkoutservice and recommendationservice downstream of productcatalogservice, and by loadgenerator traffic at the edge.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts across loadgenerator, frontend, and productcatalogservice within seconds suggests a real user-facing failure, not a single-service warning. Productcatalog is the common downstream of frontend traffic, making it the likely origin, though a bad deploy cannot be ruled out.
